title: Egg Sandwich on Biscuit with Sausage and Cheese

content.title: About
content.content: The egg sandwich on biscuit with sausage and cheese is a hearty breakfast or snack consisting of a soft biscuit, a fried egg, a flavorful sausage, and melted cheese. All ingredients are assembled into a single portable sandwich.

content.title: Interesting Facts
items: The biscuit used is typically leavened without yeast, giving it a light and airy texture.
The sausage is often made from pork or turkey and seasoned with spices such as paprika and garlic.
Cheese is usually melted briefly to create a gooey layer over the egg and sausage.
The combination of egg, meat, and dairy provides a high protein content in one serving.
Biscuit bread stays fresh longest when stored in an airtight container.

items.title: Rich in protein
items.content: Egg, sausage, and cheese together supply about 20‑25 g of protein, supporting muscle growth and repair.

items.title: Source of B‑vitamins
items.content: Eggs and meat contain vitamin B12, niacin, and riboflavin, important for energy metabolism.

items.title: Calcium and phosphorus
items.content: Cheese provides calcium and phosphorus, which are essential for bone health.

items.title: Sustained energy
items.content: Carbohydrates from the biscuit combined with fats from cheese and sausage give lasting satiety.

items.title: Contains iron
items.content: Egg and meat contain heme iron, which is more readily absorbed by the body.

items.title: High sodium content
items.content: Sausage and cheese often contain a lot of salt, which can be an issue for hypertension.

items.title: Saturated fats
items.content: Sausage and cheese are rich in saturated fats, so intake should be limited for heart‑healthy diets.

items.title: Allergy to eggs or dairy
items.content: People with egg or milk allergies may experience reactions to this sandwich.

items.title: Caloric density
items.content: One serving can contain 350‑450 kcal, so consider overall daily calorie balance.

content.title: How to Eat
content.content: The sandwich can be enjoyed hot, briefly warmed in a microwave or skillet to melt the cheese. It is convenient for a lunchbox and can be halved for children.

content.title: Storage
content.content: Store the prepared sandwich in an airtight container in the refrigerator for up to 2‑3 days. For freezing, wrap tightly in plastic wrap and keep up to 1 month, then reheat before serving.
